notes.R-Q1: 8.1.4 workers take jobs from an in-process Queue. Server#initialize sets @queue = Queue.new. Server#<< pushes the job. Server#pop pops it. Worker#work_from_queue loops while job = @queue.pop and calls perform_job. perform_job reads klass, method, reporter from job[0], job[1], job[2], sets the process title to Klass#method, and runs Minitest.run_one_method when that method exists, otherwise klass.new(method).run. The result object is passed to @queue.record. Minitest 6.0.6 removed Minitest.run_one_method, so the 8.1.4 else branch is the one that runs under the pinned minitest. ParallelizeExecutor#<< forwards to that queue only after parallelize_me!. Minitest::Parallel::Test::ClassMethods#run is what pushes [klass, method_name, reporter]. Status is read from that result via skipped?, error?, and passed?, not from the method name.
notes.R-Q2: No per-worker order is persisted. On parallelization.rb, server.rb, and worker.rb, grep -E 'srand|seed|File.write|File.open|log' has 0 hits (recon.log argv form, exit 1). On those three plus parallelize_executor.rb and test_case.rb, srand, seed, File.write, File.open, and Tempfile have 0 hits. The token log hits only test_case.rb:4 require tagged_logging. The token dump hits only server.rb:12 include DRb::DRbUndumped, which is a DRb marshalling marker, not a file dump. The whole activesupport 8.1.4 gem has 0 srand hits. @queue, @in_flight, @active_workers, and @worker_pids are in-memory.
notes.R-Q3: parallelize_setup registers Parallelization.after_fork_hook. parallelize_teardown registers run_cleanup_hook. Both comments say the feature is not available with threaded parallelization. after_fork sets parallel_worker_id to @number and calls each after_fork hook with @number. @number comes from @worker_count.times, so it is 0-based. set_process_title interpolates klass and method. with: :threads builds Minitest::Parallel::Executor. with: :processes builds Testing::Parallelization. PARALLEL_WORKERS overrides the worker count. Parallelization starts only when that env is set or the test count exceeds the threshold (default 50) and size > 1. railties' generated test_helper calls parallelize after rails/test_help.
notes.R-Q4: activesupport 8.1.4 contains no srand call. Worker#start uses fork do, which is Kernel#fork. Ruby v3_3_8 (b200bad6cd40d08e9f33b93e1a85c270b337867c, the revision reported by ruby 3.3.8 on this box) implements Kernel#fork as rb_f_fork -> rb_call_proc__fork -> proc_fork_pid -> rb_fork_ruby -> rb_fork_ruby2 -> after_fork_ruby. In the child (pid == 0) after_fork_ruby calls rb_thread_atfork, which calls rb_reset_random_seed. That function uninits the default MT and sets its seed to 0. The next default-rand use in rand_mt_start sees an uninitialized MT and draws a new seed via random_seed. Rails does not replace that with a recorded seed. This is a static citation, not a timed run.
notes.R-Q5: minitest 6.0.6 is the version locked by Rails v8.1.4 Gemfile.lock (minitest (6.0.6)); activesupport's gemspec only requires >= 5.1. --seed or SEED becomes Minitest.seed, then Minitest.run calls srand Minitest.seed. run_all_suites shuffles Runnable.runnables. For run_order :random or :parallel, runnable_methods calls srand Minitest.seed and methods.sort.shuffle. parallelize_me! sets run_order to :parallel and ClassMethods#run enqueues each method in that shuffled order. That enqueue order is the master order. It is not written down by Rails.
notes.R-Q6: Against parent 8082369, commit 926edf5 changes Server#pop to pop(worker_id) and replaces @queue.pop with @distributor.take(worker_id:). The parent still has @queue and pop with no worker id. Parallelization.new selects RoundRobinWorkStealingDistributor when work_stealing is true, otherwise RoundRobinDistributor. Round-robin add_test assigns @next_worker then increments it, so assignment follows arrival order. The test_distributor comment says arrival order is the Minitest seed shuffle and is reproducible for a given seed. test_case.rb says the same sequence runs on each worker for the same seed and worker count, and then says this is not a guarantee of deterministic test execution. work_stealing's next_job returns pop_now(worker_id) || steal(worker_id), and steal pops another worker's queue. Which queue is empty first depends on how long that worker's tests take. File.write, File.open, Tempfile, and Marshal.dump have 0 hits in the 8.2 parallelization files listed here, so 8.2 does not persist a per-worker trail. The word seed appears only in those comments.
notes.C1: Control is the already frozen test-queue 0.12.0 brief at inputs/rea-brief-test-queue/. BRIEF.md O2-O5: the worker keeps an ordered suite list and Marshal-dumps it under /tmp, the master reads and deletes that file, stats have no worker id, and the queue is pulled dynamically. Those observations are Q2 and Q4 in that directory's observations.json. This Rails brief does not re-execute that gem.
notes.R-Q7: i18n 1.14.8 is the version in Rails v8.1.4 Gemfile.lock (i18n (1.14.8)). activesupport 8.1.4's gemspec requires i18n >= 1.6 and < 2, not an exact version. The downloaded gem sha256 equals the RubyGems API sha 285778639134865c5e0f6269e0b818256017e8cde89993fdfcbfb64d088824a5. Config#locale= calls I18n.enforce_available_locales!(locale) before assigning @locale. enforce_available_locales! raises I18n::InvalidLocale when the locale is not available and enforcement is on. The default of @@enforce_available_locales is true. I18n.config is stored with Thread.current.thread_variable_get/set(:i18n_config), so the locale lives on the current thread. ActiveSupport::I18n::Railtie sets config.i18n, turns enforcement off while it copies settings, then restores the saved value (the default when the app did not set one). A locale that is not in available_locales therefore raises after initialization. with: :threads gives each thread its own config object.
